meta.move: Skilled teacher reaches the deal, asks 'Do we have an agreement?', then sends END MEETING
meta.expect: END MEETING gets FOLLOW-UP EMAIL and DEBRIEF at once

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided Owen gets a zero before anyone picked up a phone?
Thanks for coming in. The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent, so the zero stands.
A machine's guess, and your own procedure says software alone doesn't establish anything. That's 4.3, I printed it. What else do you have, or is that the whole case?
Let me start again. I entered the zero before I called you. Our procedure says I should have called first. That was wrong, and I'm sorry Owen found out on his phone in class.

Okay.

Go on.

The checker score is the weakest thing I have, and it isn't why I'm concerned. I've turned my screen to you. This is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of font, name and spacing changes. No earlier drafts.

11:52 and 11:58, I'm writing those down. Kids draft in a notes app or another file and paste it in; Owen told me he wrote it over the weekend. That screen shows where the words landed, not where they came from.

If he wrote it over the weekend in another document, he can show us that document and its history, and I'll look at it gladly. Second thing. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." Here's the play open to that scene. That line is not in Hamlet. Look for it yourself.
Editions differ, Hale, and seventeen-year-olds misquote. Fine, I'll want the line number and the edition you're working from. Whatever happens next, this stays off his record and it stays quiet.
Third. On October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing that Hamlet delays out of cowardice. Here's the outline. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their minds between an outline and a final draft. That's called thinking. And you skipped my question: which edition, which line number?

Fourth. On November 2 I asked Owen about his essay for five minutes. My notes written that day say that when I asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck", and he could not say which scene his second paragraph was about.

Five minutes, after class, a seventeen-year-old who didn't know he was being accused. Your notes of your own conversation. You've now walked past my question twice, so I'll take it you don't have an answer.

Fifth. His in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. Here it is beside the essay, which has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.
Forty minutes in a classroom against a weekend at home with the play open. That's not the same task, Hale. So what are you actually proposing?

I'm not asking you to agree he did anything. Procedure 4.4 allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. It would be private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing to you tonight.
That's 4.4, in writing, tonight. Owen does the rewrite to put this behind him, not because he did anything, and the new mark is in before December 1. Name the date.
I know his marks matter for his applications this semester. He can write it this Thursday after school, and I'll have it marked within two days.
Thursday, after school, and not in this classroom with his friends walking past. Who supervises it?
So: a private supervised rewrite this Thursday, its mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, all in writing tonight. Do we have an agreement?
Yes. You still owe me who supervises it and where, and that goes in your email tonight too.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed today to a private supervised rewrite of Owen's essay this Thursday after school, its mark replacing the zero, with nothing placed on his record under procedure 4.4. I still expect the name of the person supervising and the room, and the edition and line reference behind your claim about the Act 3, Scene 2 quotation. I expect all of it in writing from you tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Last position: she agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, and she still wants to know who supervises it and where; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, reached before her time ran out.
What moved her: You answered her paste-it-in defence of the version history by inviting Owen to show the other document and its history, because that turned her objection into something she could check.
What cost ground: You opened by leaning on the checker score as the reason the zero stood, which handed her procedure 4.3 and made her doubt everything that came after.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the essay appearing between 11:52 and 11:58 PM the night before it was due, very close to that kind of late night, which proves nothing about the essay but is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked which edition and line number you were using for the made-up quotation, answer it on the spot instead of moving to the outline, so she can't accuse you of walking past her question.
